assumptions: FY27 Revenue INR 4,500 Cr as guided
Interest costs normalize from INR 45 Cr FY26 level

projection.rationale: Revenue guided to INR 4,500 Cr for FY27, implying ~INR 950 Cr in Q1 with typical Q1 seasonality (lowest quarter). OPM at 7.0% guided band lower end as ramp-up continues; PAT benefits from vanishing interest costs.
Sequential revenue growth as execution picks up post-monsoon. OPM improves to 7.5% mid-band as low-margin ramp-up phases mature and ECL provision distortion absent.
Peak execution quarter historically; revenue scales to INR 1,200 Cr. OPM hits 8% upper guidance band on strong operating leverage. PAT rises sharply with normalized interest costs.
Year-end push to meet INR 4,500 Cr annual target. OPM moderates to 7.5% on mix of project completions and new ramp-ups. PAT steady with sustained lower interest burden.

deepdive.sec: Specialized EPC & Precast Construction (Gujarat Infrastructure & Adani Group Ecosystem)

bull_bear.body: Priority on becoming debt-free within 2-3 quarters by utilizing INR 814 Cr interest-free mobilization advances from Adani to repay INR 317 Cr gross debt. Surplus cash to be deployed in working capital and potential minor precast equipment upgrades. No dividend policy change discussed.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: High concentration risk (67% order book from Adani Group); Execution delays in Mumbai projects (Matunga, Mahim) due to regulatory approvals/tree cutting; Potential further ECL provisions on UP Medical College projects (INR 60 Cr unbilled + INR 40 Cr receivable) if settlements drag; Working capital strain if non-Adani receivables (currently ~90-100 days) do not normalize to 60 days.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on execution scale and order visibility; Conservative on margin guidance (7-8%) to account for variability; Optimistic on balance sheet repair (debt-free target) and cash flow improvement due to favorable group payment terms; Transparent regarding one-off provisions (Kashi) and legacy receivable challenges (UP, SDB).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The INR 814 Cr mobilization advance is entirely interest-free, acting as a massive working capital subsidy that will structurally lower finance costs to near-zero, effectively converting previous interest expenses (INR 45 Cr) directly into PAT. The 'margin compression' is largely an accounting artifact of front-loading provisions and ramp-up costs, masking the underlying cash profitability of the new order mix.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Comfortable leverage at 0.25x including mobilisation advance, with a working capital cycle of 94 days as on FY26.
- Credit rating of CARE A+ (Stable) / CARE A1, supporting bid capacity for high-value contracts.
- Equity has been raised selectively for growth — ₹211.68 crore at the May-2017 NSE/BSE listing and ₹244 crore via QIP in April 2024.
- The Adani partnership is expected to enhance balance-sheet strength, improve access to capital and lower working-capital and receivable-related risks over time.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Institutional (Gati Shakti Univ, Science City), Industrial (Airport dev, Fintech building), Residential (GIFT City high-rise, Matunga rehab), Government (Sabarmati Riverfront, Dharoi Dam). Precast facility utilization high; executed 122m residential tower and Project 90 (18 floors in 148 days).
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need for rapid, high-quality construction of massive industrial and institutional projects in Gujarat with complex timelines. | Adani Enterprises Ltd | beneficiary | High | PSP Projects acts as a critical execution arm for Adani's capex surge (Airport, GIFT City, Temple), offering specialized precast speed and financial flexibility via interest-free advances. |
| Intense competition for large government infrastructure tenders in Western India. | Generic Regional EPC Peers | loser | Med | PSP's locked-in 67% order book from Adani and specialized precast moat may crowd out smaller peers from marquee Gujarat projects like Ambaji Temple and Sabarmati Riverfront. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Integrated one-stop EPC contractor spanning the full value chain — design, construction, MEP, interior fit-outs and O&M — giving single-point accountability, faster project turnaround and the ability to bid larger, more complex projects.
- Diversified across industrial, institutional, government, government-residential and residential segments, with construction presence in Gujarat, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and New Delhi.
- Pre-qualification credentials have compounded with each landmark delivered (Surat Diamond Bourse, Kashi Vishwanath Dham, GIFT City high-rises), taking the company into the league of handling projects up to ₹2,500 crore and letting it compete alongside India's leading construction companies.
- Repeat-order franchise built on trust: 100+ private and public clients, with 73 projects for the Adani Group, 30 for Zydus Cadila, 16 for Torrent and 10 for Sabarmati Riverfront.
- Founder-led by a first-generation civil engineer with 40+ years of experience, with a second-generation family management team in CEO and Executive Director roles.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Adani stake] Adani Infra (India) Limited acquired a 34.41% stake through an Open Offer and Share Purchase Agreement and joined the promoter group, following the Nov-2024 agreement to acquire up to 30.07% from existing promoters.
- [Governance] The partnership brings board representation and aligned long-term interests, with management describing sharper execution focus on project planning, quality and technology adoption.
- [Client concentration] With ~70% of the project mix and 61% of the bid book being within-group, a growing share of business now originates from the Adani ecosystem.
- [Recognition] Awarded 2025 GROHE HURUN INDIA 'Pioneer in infrastructure development and engineering', plus repeated 'Fastest Growing Construction Company' honours at the Construction World Annual Awards.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: FY26 margin compression (6% vs 7.1% prior) due to low-margin ramp-up phase of large projects and INR 29 Cr ECL provision. FY27 guidance 7-8% supported by pass-through material contracts with Adani (mitigating inflation/war risk) and operating leverage. Employee cost expected to grow in line with revenue (2-4% of sales) as hiring stabilizes.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue: INR 4,500 Cr for FY27. EBITDA Margin: 7-8% band. Order Inflow: INR 5,000-6,000 Cr from Adani Group + INR 1,000-2,000 Cr external potential. Capex: INR 120-150 Cr (approx. 3% of revenue).
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: INR 13,447 Cr total; 67% (INR 9,000 Cr) from Adani Group, 33% (INR 4,300 Cr) external. Key projects: Shree Ambaji Mata Temple (INR 966 Cr), SMC Highrise (INR 731 Cr), GIFT City Fintech Building (INR 261 Cr), Human & Biological Science Gallery (INR 254 Cr), Sabarmati River Front Phase II (INR 218 Cr), Dharoi Dam Region (INR 223 Cr). Bid pipeline: INR 6,600 Cr (60% group, 40% external).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Upside from Commonwealth Games stadium tender (INR 7,000-8,000 Cr potential, expected soon); expansion of precast capacity with minimal capex (INR 15-20 Cr for equipment) if order flow exceeds 3M sqft/year; penetration into non-Gujarat markets via large institutional bids.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: PSP Projects delivered record Q4 revenue (INR 1,115 Cr, +66% YoY) and a massive order book (INR 13,447 Cr, +85% YoY) driven by Adani Group mandates, though FY26 margins compressed to 6% due to project mix and a INR 29 Cr one-off ECL provision. The core investment thesis pivots to FY27 margin expansion (7-8% EBITDA) and PAT recovery as mobilization advances eliminate interest costs, targeting a debt-free status within 2-3 quarters.

open.item: Working capital cycle, which rose to 102 days from 65 days, is expected to stabilise in Q3FY26 helped by Adani mobilisation advances and October collections.
Precast erection for Adani projects starts with one project next month and three more Shantigram precast projects by December 2025 (four Adani precast projects in hand).
open.promised: 1 project in Nov 2025 + 3 more by Dec 2025 count of projects

open.item: Dharoi Dam project has two pending land acquisition components expected to be finalised by November 2025, with paused horizontal development work now resumed.

Company intends to bid for marquee non-Adani projects - Commonwealth Games (Ahmedabad 2030), stadiums and Somnath-type temple projects sized above Rs 800-1,000 crore, with tenders expected after Diwali.
Labour availability has normalised after the Q1FY26 shortfall, though a 10%-12% shortfall is expected around Diwali; management says labour will no longer be a constraint.
Fund-based bank working capital utilisation is expected to reduce drastically by end of Q3FY26, aided by minimum Rs 750 crores of mobilisation advance (5%-10%) on Rs 7,500 crores of Adani orders.
Management reiterated an EBITDA margin guidance range of 8% to 9%, expected to be visible from Q2FY26 or at the latest Q3FY26.
A further Dharavi (Matunga block) project of around Rs 2,000 crore is under discussion and should close before March 2026.
Closing FY26 order book guidance was cut to Rs 11,000-12,000 crore from the earlier Rs 14,000-15,000 crore, on Rs 9,178 crore outstanding plus Rs 2,000-3,000 crore of expected Q4 wins.
Around Rs 2,000-3,000 crore of further order inflow is expected by March 2026, excluding the Rs 965 crore Adani order already booked in Q3.
FY26 capex will total about Rs 200 crore -- Rs 153 crore spent in 9M plus a further Rs 40-50 crore in Q4 -- mainly shuttering, cranes and equipment for Adani projects.
The Rs 8 crore employee-cost hit from the new Labour Code (past service cost for gratuity/leave encashment) is a one-time effect with no impact from Q4FY26 onwards.
PSP has emerged lowest bidder on the Rs 965 crore Ambaji Corridor / temple development project and is awaiting the award.
PSP won a favourable arbitral award against BMCMC for Rs 61.44 crore principal plus 9% interest payable within 60 days (11% thereafter), totalling about Rs 80 crore expected by March.
On the Rs 1,300 crore Mahim (Dharavi) project, excavation will be completed within about a month and foundation work should start by March 2026, lifting revenue thereafter.
Depreciation should continue at Rs 24-25 crore per quarter going forward given Rs 153 crore of asset additions this year.
Management said the near-term quarterly EBITDA margin should be near 7%-8%, noting Q3 was 6.73% only because of a 1% hit from the new Labour Code.
Management reiterated FY26 revenue guidance of Rs 3,100-3,200 crore, saying finishing-stage projects will make it up by March.
Q4FY26 revenue run-rate is expected at Rs 1,100-1,200 crore to reach the full-year guidance.
Outstanding order book is targeted at Rs 14,000-15,000 crore by March 2026 (gross book could touch Rs 16,000 crore before revenue burn).
